content: Polyethylene glycol-electrolyte solution (PEG-ES) is a laxative approved by the FDA for bowel cleansing prior to colonoscopy. Common side effects include abdominal bloating, fullness, and nausea. For adults, the recommended oral dosage is 240 mL (8 oz.) every 10 minutes until the rectal effluent is clear or a total of 4 liters is consumed. Off-label adult use includes taking 1 liter orally in two 500 mL portions within 4 to 6 hours or 1000 mL every 45 to 75 minutes. For pediatric patients aged 6 months or older, the oral dosage is 25 mL/kg/hour until the rectal effluent is clear. Rapid consumption of each portion is preferred over continuous small sips. Nasogastric tube administration is also an option at the same rate. PEG-ES is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to its components, ileus, gastrointestinal obstruction, gastric retention, bowel perforation, toxic colitis, or toxic megacolon. It should be used cautiously in patients with severe ulcerative colitis and in children under 2 years of age due to the risk of hypoglycemia, as the solution contains no caloric substrate. Dehydration and hypokalemia have been reported in pediatric cases. Patients with impaired gag reflex, unconscious or semiconscious states, or those prone to regurgitation or aspiration should be closely monitored during administration, especially via nasogastric tube. If severe bloating, distension, or abdominal pain occurs, administration should be slowed or temporarily stopped. Suspected gastrointestinal obstruction or perforation should be ruled out before use. The most common adverse reactions include nausea, abdominal fullness, and bloating, occurring in up to 50% of patients. Less frequent reactions include abdominal cramps, vomiting, and anal irritation. Rare allergic reactions such as urticaria, rhinitis, dermatitis, and anaphylaxis have been reported. Serious adverse events, including upper GI bleeding, esophageal perforation, asystole, and pulmonary complications, have been documented in patients over 60 years of age. PEG-ES induces diarrhea to cleanse the bowel, typically within four hours. Its osmotic activity and electrolyte composition result in minimal net absorption or excretion of ions or water, allowing large volumes to be administered without significant fluid or electrolyte imbalance. The solution is supplied as a powdered form in a 4-liter bottle with optional flavor packs. It should be stored at 25°C (77°F) with permissible excursions between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). Once reconstituted, the solution must be refrigerated and used within 48 hours, with any unused portion discarded. Patients should avoid solid food for 3 to 4 hours before drinking the solution and should not consume solid food within 2 hours of administration. Adults should drink 240 mL every 10 minutes until the stool is clear, typically requiring at least 3 liters. Pediatric patients should drink 25 mL/kg/hour until the stool is clear. Rapid consumption is preferred, and the first bowel movement usually occurs about one hour after starting the solution. Alcohol interaction with PEG-ES has not been established, and patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name TRILYTE®.
